supersededBy.reason: Subjects changed after the #336 review; see the successor. Nothing below was edited.

supersedes.defect: That sweep rewrote only the current mutant's file from its pristine copy and restored every subject only once, at the end. When the sweep moved to the next file, the last mutant of the previous file stayed applied: prompts.ts mutant 32 (discovery-instructions-swapped) was live for every provider-draft.ts and discovery-provider.ts mutant (indexes 33-61), and provider-draft.ts mutant 45 for every discovery-provider.ts mutant (46-61). Those runs failed on the contaminating mutant's digest pins, so their kills say nothing about their own predicate; number-type-unchecked (index 41) is equivalent and only read as killed because of it.

method: Before every mutant the runner rewrites every subject from its committed bytes, checks each subject's sha256 against the commit, and runs the unmutated battery (`npx vitest run` over the four test files), which must pass with no failure. It then replaces exactly one occurrence of `old` with `new` in `file` (applied only when `old` occurs exactly once), runs the battery, and restores and re-checks every subject. Killed means the run exited non-zero with at least one failed test.
